**AILANG Parse** is an open-source document parsing engine that converts
   office documents, PDFs, emails, and media files into a unified
   *Block ADT* (Algebraic Data Type). It runs natively, in the browser via WASM,
   and as a cloud API.

Most document parsers are format-specific black boxes.
  AILANG Parse gives you

for 16+ formats —
  deterministic for office files, AI-powered for PDFs and media — with
  typed errors, cost metadata, and full replayability.

`# Python
pip install ailang-parse

# JavaScript / TypeScript
npm install @sunholo/ailang-parse

# Go
go get github.com/sunholo-data/ailang-parse-go`

`# Python example
from ailang_parse import parse

result = parse("quarterly_report.docx", output="markdown")
print(result.text)        # Markdown output
print(result.blocks)      # Structured Block ADT
print(result.metadata)    # Page count, word count, images found`

**Tip:** For deterministic formats (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, HTML, CSV, Markdown),
     no API key is needed. AI-powered formats (PDF, images, audio, video) require
     a Gemini or Anthropic API key.
Every parsed document becomes a list of **Blocks**. There are 9 block variants:

rows: Tabular data with rows and cells

blocks.text: These parsers produce identical output for the same input, every time:

items:
**DOCX** — Word documents with full fidelity
    

Tables with merged cells and styles
Track changes (insertions, deletions, moves)
Comments with author attribution
Headers, footers, and footnotes
Embedded images (PNG, JPEG, EMF, WMF)
Tables with merged cells and styles

**PPTX** — PowerPoint presentations
    

Slide content with speaker notes
Tables and shapes
Master slide layouts

**XLSX** — Excel spreadsheets
    

Multiple sheets as sections
Formulas (cached values)
Merged cells and number formats

blocks.text: These use multimodal AI (Gemini or Claude) for extraction:

blocks.description: AILANG Parse architecture diagram showing document input flowing through format detection, parser selection, and Block ADT output

blocks.text: Figure 1: Document processing pipeline — from raw file to structured blocks
The processing pipeline has four stages:

Identifies the input format by MIME type and file extension. ZIP-based formats
      (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, EPUB, ODT) are detected by inspecting archive contents.

Routes to the appropriate parser module. Deterministic parsers handle
      structured formats; AI parsers handle visual/audio content.

The parser converts format-specific structures (XML elements, table cells,
      slide shapes) into the universal Block ADT.

Blocks are serialized to the requested output format: JSON (structured),
      Markdown (human-readable), HTML (web-ready), or
      [A2UI](https://sunholo.com/ailang-parse/a2ui) (agent-friendly).
